body:
More context: the XML file is created by the test runners or by default by test-setup.sh. The test time out is done by the process wrapper which run that test runner. So it's not really clear if there is a good way to do it.

I think we could add an intercept in the test-setup.sh on interrupt but I don't know how reliable that would be. I guess trying (it's not hard) and running the bazel test suite should be enough to say.

Any update on this? Test timeouts are becoming more of an issue for me and it'd be great if I could easily track them down using the XML file.

I could probably make it happen with a `--run_under` script but that smells kinda funny to me.

Maybe the test strategy should write an XML file if the test didn't write one? We send a SIGTERM signal on timeout, but there may be other reasons for sending SIGTERM, like Ctrl-C on the command-line, so the test may not be able to reliably distinguish between those.

That's the approach we have right now but that codes live in test-setup.sh
and we might want to move that in the calling process instead. The code
that write the default XML file get killed by the time out.

On Wed, Feb 15, 2017 at 10:54 AM Ulf Adams <notifications@github.com> wrote:

> Maybe the test strategy should write an XML file if the test didn't write
> one? We send a SIGTERM signal on timeout, but there may be other reasons
> for sending SIGTERM, like Ctrl-C on the command-line, so the test may not
> be able to reliably distinguish between those.
>

Ah, yes. When I said 'test strategy' I actually literally meant the TestStrategy class in Bazel, which is the calling code.

If this is with the Java test runner, maybe we should update the test runner to write the xml file when it gets a SIGTERM. That way you get all the passed tests in the XML, and the current test could maybe be automatically marked as timeout. I wonder why we aren't seeing this issue with our internal test runner, maybe the code isn't completely identical?
This is a bug in the sandbox. It works if I specify --spawn_strategy=processwrapper-sandbox but not if I specify --spawn_strategy=linux-sandbox.

The link is: http://ci.bazel.io/blue/organizations/jenkins/CR%2Fbazel-tests/detail/bazel-tests/141/pipeline/

1. The link goes to the entire pipeline, which isn't useful. It took me a while to realize I need to click the "Tests" at the top right to see the actual results.
2. The "Tests" tab says that all tests pass. So why is the change marked UNSTABLE? I can't determine that anywhere.

body: I think the sandbox kills the subprocess rather than sending it SIGTERM.

Yes, linux-sandbox.cc terminates its child by relying on the kernel to kill it via PR_SET_PDEATHSIG with SIGKILL. Instead it should first try to kill its child process with SIGTERM and only after a timeout exit (and thus trigger SIGKILL). I'll send a fix for it later.

issue.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:
When a test times out, the stdout and stderr from the underlying test is not written to the console. I noticed that changes were made to write stdout and stderr to the XML test output file on a timeout as per https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/1027. In addition to the XML test output file, I'd like test-setup.sh write to the console.

Here is an example test.
